name: Firebase Crashlytics

dataTypes.type: App info and performance / Crash logs
dataTypes.when: Always: stack traces are collected when the app crashes. Also any developer-recorded non-fatal events with custom stack traces.

Always: relevant application state and point-in-time device metadata at crash time; the transitively included Firebase sessions SDK also collects app metadata, device metadata (manufacturer, model) and usage metrics such as foreground time.

dataTypes.type: Device or other IDs / Device or other IDs
dataTypes.when: Always: Crashlytics generates and stores a Crashlytics installation UUID to measure users affected by a crash. Firebase installation ID (FID), a per-installation identifier, collected by the transitively included Firebase installations SDK (com.google.firebase:firebase-installations).
Only if the app attaches a user ID to crash reports (setUserId).

ask: Do you call setUserId() on Crashlytics? If no, remove Personal info / User IDs.
Do you attach custom keys or logs (setCustomKey / log) to crash reports? If they contain personal data (email, name, location, content), declare those data types too.
Do you also include Google Analytics for Firebase? Crashlytics then uses Analytics 'breadcrumb' logs (user actions before a crash); make sure the firebase-analytics entry is declared.
Do you also include Remote Config? Crashlytics then collects Remote Config rollout metadata (developer-defined).

sources.title: Prepare for Google Play's data disclosure requirements (Firebase)

notes: Purposes are our mapping: Firebase says the data is used 'to enable crash reporting and crash management services'. Some developers also select App functionality; Analytics is the usual Play mapping for crash diagnostics. Depends on firebase-installations and firebase-sessions (both transitive), whose data is folded in above. Firebase's page does not give a per-product collected/shared table; it states globally that Firebase does not transfer the listed data to third parties except to subprocessors that help provide Firebase services or per the developer's instructions (e.g. linking to non-Firebase services). On that basis shared=false and role=service-provider. The page lists raw data items (e.g. 'stack traces', 'IP address'), not Play data-type labels; the mapping to Play labels and purposes here is ours.
